messages.text:
having an issue loading harlo os onto my bc04.  I get Error: Invalid head of packet (0x45): Possible serial noise or corruption. and it will not progress.  install log looks like this:

Detecting chip type... 
ESP32-S3
Chip Revision: 0
Chip is ESP32-S3 (QFN56) (revision v0.2)
Features: Wi-Fi,BLE,Embedded PSRAM 8MB (AP_3v3)
Crystal is 40MHz
MAC: ····
Uploading stub...
Running stub...
Hard resetting via RTS pin...
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill
Searched the web · esptool "Invalid head of packet (0x45)" serial noise ESP32-S
Read harlolabs.com
Searched the web · Harlo OS install guide harlolabs flash Hammer BC04 ESP32-S3

Hi, I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed your flashing question to me.

Good news: your log shows the board is fine. The flasher found the chip (ESP32-S3, 8MB PSRAM) and uploaded the stub, so the USB link works. It fails right after "Hard resetting via RTS pin", which is where the board should stay in download mode and instead reboots normally.

What the error means: 
the 0x45 is the first byte of the chip's own boot banner ("ESP-ROM:esp32..."), so the flasher is reading plain boot text where it expects a data packet
. That is the known esptool behaviour reported on 
Espressif's own issue tracker for this exact message
, not a dead board.

First check, one thing only. Put the BC04 into download mode by hand instead of letting the tool reset it:

1. Unplug the unit and close any other tab, serial monitor or app that has the port open.
2. Plug the USB cable straight into the computer (no hub, no extension, no front panel splitter), and make sure it is a data cable, not a charge-only one.
3. Hold the BOOT button on the control board, plug the USB in while holding, keep holding about 2 seconds, then release.
4. In the flasher at harlolabs.com (Chrome or Edge), reconnect to the port and run Erase first, then Install.

Tell me what happens after that, and also tell me:
- which operating system you are on
- whether you are flashing through the harlolabs.com web flasher or esptool on the command line

If it still stops at the same point, the next step is dropping the baud rate (115200) and a different USB port or cable, which clears most of these.
which button is the boot button on the bc04?
Let me check that rather than guess at a button on your board.
Searched the web · Hammer BC04 miner BOOT button ESP32-S3 flash firmware contro

Honest answer: I do not want to point you at the wrong button, and the BC04's control board is a small ESP32-S3 module behind the screen, so the button layout depends on which revision you have.

Two things that help right away:

1. If you can, send me a photo of the board around the USB-C port (screen off if you already removed it). I will tell you exactly which of the two small buttons is BOOT on your revision.
2. On these ESP32-S3 boards there are normally two tiny buttons flanking the USB-C port: one is BOOT (GPIO0), one is RESET. The sequence is: hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT, then click Connect in the flasher. If you hold the wrong one the board just reboots, nothing breaks, so trying both in turn is safe.

While you get that photo, there is a second route that often fixes this error without any button at all, since your board is already talking to the flasher:

- Use a different USB data cable and a rear USB port straight on the machine
- In the flasher, set the baud rate to 115200 if it offers the choice
- Run Erase first, then Install

Which one do you want to try first, the photo or the lower baud retry?
I'm using the web flasher

Good, that narrows it. The web flasher (esptool-js over Web Serial) has no baud setting to drop, so the lower baud route is out and the manual download mode is the fix that matters here.

Do this in order:

1. Fully power cycle the miner: unplug USB and the power brick, wait 10 seconds, plug the power back in.
2. Close every other Chrome or Edge tab that has the flasher open, and any serial monitor. Only one window may hold the port.
3. Plug the USB cable into a port straight on the computer, not a hub or a monitor.
4. Hold the small button next to the USB-C port down while you click Connect in the flasher, and keep it held until the chip info line appears.
5. Then run Erase, then Install, and leave the unit alone while it works.

If step 4 is the one you are unsure about: send me a photo of the board around the USB-C port and I will name the exact button for your revision. Both buttons are safe to press, the wrong one just reboots the board.

One more thing I need from you either way: which operating system are you on, Windows, macOS or Linux? On Windows this error is very often the USB serial driver (CP210x or CH340) rather than the board, and that is a two minute fix.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that photo tells me what I needed.

What I see: the Hammer BC04 main board with the LilyGO style display module mounted on the left, screen on and showing W:192.168.201.201, BC04, Hashrate 0 Th/s, 41.6 C, BD 751.3M, uptime 0h 0m, so the unit just booted. Power is coming in through the yellow XT connector top right, and the board is silkscreened HAMMER / BC04 with the Ethernet jack on the left.

The buttons you need are on the display module itself, the small black square tact switches to the right of the screen, one directly above the USB-C port and one directly below it. Those two are your BOOT and RESET. On these modules the one below the USB-C port (the one nearest the HAMMER silkscreen) is normally BOOT.

Try this:

1. Leave the power connected as it is now.
2. Plug the USB-C cable into the port between those two buttons, straight into the computer.
3. Hold the lower button down, and keep holding it while you click Connect in the web flasher.
4. Keep holding until the chip info line appears in the log, then release and run Erase, then Install.

If the log still ends at "Hard resetting via RTS pin", repeat the exact same sequence with the upper button instead. One of the two is BOOT, and pressing the wrong one only reboots the miner.

Still need one thing from you: Windows, macOS or Linux?
macos

macOS is useful to know, two things behave differently there:

1. In the Chrome or Edge port dialog, pick the port that reads cu.usbserial... or cu.usbmodem... If you picked anything else (Bluetooth-Incoming-Port shows up for a lot of people), the flasher connects to nothing useful and dies exactly where yours does. Safari cannot do this at all, it has no Web Serial, so it must be Chrome or Edge.
2. On recent Macs a USB-C to USB-C cable straight into the machine is often the problem. If you have a USB-A to USB-C cable plus a simple A adapter or dock, that path is noticeably more reliable for ESP32-S3 flashing.

So the next attempt, in this order:

1. Chrome, one tab only, flasher page reloaded.
2. USB-A to USB-C cable if you have one.
3. Hold the lower button next to the USB-C port, click Connect while holding, release once the chip info appears.
4. Erase, then Install.

Tell me what the log says this time, the last three or four lines are enough. If it dies at the same point even with the button held, that points at the cable or the port rather than the board, and I will have you confirm the port name macOS is showing.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That picture explains the whole thing.

What I see: the Chrome dialog "harlolabs.com wants to connect to a serial port" listing SDMBP23JH, cu.Bluetooth-Incoming-Port, cu.SDMBP23JH, cu.debug-console, and at the bottom, highlighted, "USB JTAG/serial debug unit (cu.usbmodem83401) - Paired".

So you are picking the right port. That bottom one is your BC04. But it also tells me you are connected through the ESP32-S3's built in USB JTAG/serial, not through a separate USB serial chip, and that is exactly why your flash dies at "Hard resetting via RTS pin".

Why: on native USB, the reset makes the chip disconnect and re-enumerate as a USB device. The browser's hold on cu.usbmodem83401 dies with it, and the flasher reads the boot banner (your 0x45) instead of a reply. It is a USB enumeration problem, not a bad board.

The fix is to get the board into download mode before you connect, so it never has to reset:

1. Unplug the USB-C cable. Leave the power on.
2. Hold the lower button next to the USB-C port and keep holding it.
3. While still holding, plug the USB-C cable back in. Hold about 3 more seconds, then release.
4. In Chrome, open the flasher fresh and click Connect. Pick the USB JTAG/serial debug unit entry again. Note it may now show a different number than 83401, that is normal and is the sign you are in download mode.
5. Run Erase, then Install, and do not touch anything until it finishes.

If the port does not reappear in the list at step 4, tell me and we will try the upper button for step 2 instead.
same results
Handed to the team · Harlo OS web flash on a Hammer BC04 fails at the same point after every check I

We have now ruled out the usual suspects: right port, right browser, single tab, direct USB, power cycle, and manual download mode on the button. That is as far as I can take it remotely, so I have passed the full detail to JD, our hardware lead, with your log, your model and everything we tried. The team picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email.

Faster route if you do not want to wait: our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , and mention @nullhashrate (that is JD). He and the community are very active there on weekends, and this is exactly his area.

Two things worth trying in the meantime, since both are free:

1. A different USB-C cable, and ideally a different computer. A cable that charges and even enumerates the port can still fail mid flash, and a second machine clears macOS out of the picture completely.
2. The same sequence but holding the upper button instead of the lower one at the moment you plug the USB in. We confirmed the two tact switches beside the USB-C port, but not which of them is BOOT on your revision, and holding the wrong one would produce exactly what you are seeing.

If either of those changes the log, send me the last few lines and I will pick it straight back up.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Same dialog again, and that is actually informative: the list still shows "USB JTAG/serial debug unit (cu.usbmodem83401) - Paired", the same entry as before, so the board is enumerating exactly as it did in normal mode.

One quick way to tell whether the button trick worked at all, no flasher needed: in real download mode the BC04 does not run its firmware, so the screen stays dark. If the mining screen (hashrate, temperature, BD) lights up after you plug the USB in while holding the button, the board booted normally and never entered download mode.

So, check this one thing for me:

1. Hold the lower button next to the USB-C port.
2. While holding, plug the USB-C cable in.
3. Keep holding 3 seconds, release, and look at the screen.

Tell me: does the screen stay dark, or does it light up with the mining display?

If it lights up, repeat with the upper button and tell me what the screen does then. The button that leaves the screen dark is your BOOT button, and from there the flash should run.

Your case is already with JD with the full log, and the team picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET with the answer going to your email. The Discord is the quicker path if you want it today: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.
neither button appears to put it in boot mode

Good data point, thank you. That tells me the auto reset and the buttons are both failing to hold the chip in download mode, so pushing harder on the same route is not worth your afternoon.

Two things left that I would try, in this order.

1. Flash with the main power unplugged, USB only.
Right now the board is powered from the yellow XT connector, so the firmware keeps running and restarting the chip underneath the flasher. Try:
- Unplug the XT power lead, so the miner is off.
- Plug only the USB-C cable into the display module. The screen should come up on USB power alone.
- In Chrome, Connect, pick the USB JTAG/serial debug unit entry, then Erase, then Install.
This alone clears a lot of these, because the ASIC side is not powered and nothing is fighting the reset.

2. The O. route, no USB at all.
Your miner is reachable on your network at 192.168.201.201. Open that address in a browser on the same network and look for the firmware or system update section in the stock Hammer UI. If harlolabs.com offers a downloadable BC04 image file (rather than only the browser flasher), you can upload it there and skip serial entirely. Have a look at what harlolabs.com offers for the BC04 under downloads, and tell me what file types you see. I do not want to name a file I have not verified for your model.

Tell me how number 1 goes, that is the quick one. JD has the full history already and the team picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET by email, and the Discord is there if you want eyes on it today: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.
yep, there is an ota image there

That is the better path for your unit anyway, since OTA needs no serial at all.

Before you upload, tell me exactly what the download gives you, because these images come in two shapes:
- a single firmware file (something like esp-miner.bin or a BC04 OTA .bin)
- or a pair, firmware plus a separate web UI file (often www.bin)

If it is a pair, both go in, firmware first, and the order matters.

While you check, get the conditions right, because an interrupted OTA is the one way to actually brick this:

1. Power the miner from its normal XT power lead, not USB, and leave it powered the whole time.
2. Put it on Ethernet if you can. Your screen showed Wi-Fi, and a wireless drop mid upload is the usual cause of a failed OTA.
3. Open http://192.168.201.201 in a browser on the same network, and find the firmware or upgrade section in the system settings.
4. Do not reboot, unplug or close the tab until it reports success and restarts on its own.

Send me the file name or names you downloaded and I will confirm the order before you hit upload.
looks like a single ota.bin

Single ota.bin is simple, nothing to sequence. One thing to confirm first: that you downloaded it from the BC04 device profile on harlolabs.com, not from another model's page. The B. boards do not share a pinout, so the wrong model's image boots but will not drive the ASIC.

If it is the BC04 image, go ahead:

1. Miner on its normal XT power, Ethernet if you can manage it.
2. http://192.168.201.201 in your browser, system or settings, firmware update.
3. Pick ota.bin, upload, then leave it completely alone. No reboot, no unplug, no closing the tab.
4. It restarts itself when it is done. First boot after a firmware change takes longer than usual, give it a couple of minutes before you judge it.

After it comes back, tell me what the screen shows and whether the web UI looks like Harlo OS. Then I will walk you through the pool settings so it actually starts hashing, since your screen was showing 0 Th/s.
wait, it offers a factory image and an ota image

Good catch, and the distinction matters here.

- Factory image: the complete flash, bootloader, partition table and app together, written over USB at offset 0x0. That is what the web flasher writes, and it is the one that keeps failing for you.
- OTA image: just the application, uploaded through the running miner's own web UI into its spare OTA slot. No USB, no download mode, no serial at all.

You want the OTA image, the one you already have. Keep the factory image for later if you ever do get USB flashing working, it is also the recovery route.

So:

1. Miner on its normal XT power, Ethernet if possible.
2. http://192.168.201.201, system or settings, firmware update.
3. Upload the OTA image, then leave it alone until it reboots on its own.

One honest caveat: going from stock Hammer firmware to Harlo OS over OTA works when the partition layout matches, and harlolabs publishing an OTA image for the BC04 is a good sign that it does. If the UI rejects the file or the upload fails validation, stop there and tell me rather than retrying, and do not pull the power.

Tell me what happens.

[WebSocket] Connection successful.
[2026-10-26 01:25:04] I (514587) http_server: OTA-ENC: START content_len=2497840
[2026-10-26 01:25:04] W (514597) http_server: OTA-ENC: FAIL invalid type_flag 0xE9
[2026-10-26 01:25:04] W (514597) httpd_txrx: httpd_resp_send_err: 400 Bad Request - Invalid file type
Let me check that exact log line before I tell you what it means.
Searched the web · ESP32 image magic byte 0xE9 esp_image_header magic OTA "inva
Searched the web · Hammer BC04 firmware OTA encrypted image header type_flag es

Thanks, that log line is actually the clearest thing we have had all afternoon.

Reading it: the miner's updater is the "OTA-ENC" path, meaning the stock Hammer firmware only accepts an encrypted, vendor packed update container. It checked the first byte of your file, found 0xE9, which is the magic byte of a plain unencrypted ESP application image, and refused it with 400 Bad Request. It rejected the file at the header, before writing a single byte, so your miner is untouched and perfectly fine.

What that means: the OTA image on harlolabs.com is for units already running Harlo OS, updating in place. Coming from the stock Hammer firmware, the factory image over USB is the only way in. There is no file you can upload through the stock web UI that will get you there.

So we are back to USB, which is exactly what is in JD's hands with your full log.

What is worth your time before then:

1. A different computer, ideally not a Mac. Same cable, same board, different host. That one test separates the board from macOS, and the native USB JTAG path on recent macOS is my main suspect.
2. A different USB-C cable if you have one spare.

What I would not do: keep retrying the OTA upload, or go looking for unofficial images for this board. Nothing will pass that header check, and third party firmware is not something I can support or recommend on a unit under warranty.

JD has it all, the team picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email. If you want it solved today, the Discord is the fast lane: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate. He knows the BC04 download mode quirk better than anyone.
